properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-02 (0.77.0), limitation 8, which the report left "not yet measured": CONFIRMED and worse than stated. Through `--call`, a claim is `gone` by the next call and excluded from overlaps, so two door agents claiming the same region see no collision. writes_for answers "credited … until the session ends" and the next call's write carries no author. mint_seat says "Tracked … live while the session is running"
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent A, on limitation 8 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("Each call is a fresh session. Session-scoped state (seats, claim liveness) does not carry between calls. Not yet measured."). Scratch store, one `--call` per line, isolated HOME. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-A/measure.log (L8-*).

① OBSERVED:
1. `--call mint_seat`, twice → two different seats (`host:<pid>:<rand>`, the pid being that call's process). Each says `liveness_of_this_seat`: "Tracked. This process serves exactly this session, so a claim carrying this seat reads `live` while the session is running and `gone` once it is not", and `carry_it`: "Pass this as `seat` on claim_region for the rest of this session."
2. `--call claim_region` carrying the seat from call 1 → the reply itself says `liveness: "gone"` (the minting process had exited).
3. `--call claim_report` in the next call → that claim listed with `liveness: gone`, under `stale`, `overlaps: []`.
4. `--call claim_region` with NO seat → reply `liveness: "live"` (its own pid, alive while answering). Then who:colleague claimed the SAME seed and depth in the next call, also "live".
5. `--call claim_report` → both claims `gone`, both under `stale`, `overlaps: []`. The served text says gone claims are "excluded from overlaps". Two contributors on the same ground produce no warning.
6. `--call writes_for {"contributor_id":"who:tester"}` → exit 0, `scope`: "this session — every node it writes from now on is credited to this contributor as author, until the session ends or writes_for is called again". The next `--call add_requirement` → exit 0. `--export` shows the new requirement has NO AUTHORED_BY edge; the only edges are the two CLAIMS.

② PRECEDENT: dec:stateless-seat-handle (mint-and-carry, with a refusal backstop for sessionless transports); req:seat-identity-survives-stateless-mcp; fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22 (claims read gone, by another route).

③/④ CANDIDATES: (a) the door simply starts a new session per call (the reporter's reading); (b) the server cannot tell the door is sessionless, so it answers as though state will last; (c) liveness is keyed to a process id, so no seat can outlive a one-shot process.
All three hold, and (b) and (c) are the cause behind (a). (b): the refusals that exist for exactly this case (claim without a seat; writes_for, "refused loudly … would vanish with this request") fire only on the negotiated stateless revision, and the in-process client negotiated 2025-11-25. (c): measured in step 2, where even a carried seat reads gone at once.

⑥ CLASS: session-scoped state with a guard keyed to the TRANSPORT's statelessness, met by a client whose statelessness comes from PROCESS lifetime. Every session-scoped thing the server offers is affected: seats, claims, writes_for, acting agent. The served replies promise continuity ("for the rest of this session", "until the session ends") that a door caller cannot have. The door also cannot use the per-request route writes_for names (`_meta` "reflow2/writes_for"): call_over_pipe sends arguments only. So today a door write cannot be credited to a person at all, unless an automated_agent Contributor's handle matches the client name `reflow2-mcp --call`.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether main (rmcp 3.5.0, #650) still negotiates a session-ful revision for the in-process client. Measured on 0.77.0 only. Fix options are not chosen here. Two candidates: the door declares itself per-request (so the existing refusals fire), or a durable seat handle that is not a pid, which dec:stateless-seat-handle does not provide for a process that exits.
